title: The regular module localization colimit
statement: Let R be a sheaf of commutative rings on a small site and s a global section. Use the module sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. The sequence of regular R-module sheaves whose transition is multiplication by s has a colimit c, with an isomorphism c.pt to the localized R-module sheaf carrying its zeroth coprojection to the localization unit.

source.place: Tag 03CY (module sheafification); algebra.tex Tag 00CM (localization by powers)

proof.text: At each site object apply the module localization filtered-colimit comparison to the regular module. Its fraction formula sends the stage-n element r to r times invSelf(s)^n. The naturality of the localized ring maps makes these maps a presheaf cocone; evaluation jointly reflects colimits.

For a sheaf target the module sheafification adjunction extends the presheaf descent uniquely. The adjunction unit and the presheaf colimit equations verify factorization and uniqueness. The stage-zero fraction map is the given localization unit.

theorem scalarLocalization_regularColimit
    (s : (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections) :
    ∃ c : Cocone (Functor.ofSequence (X := fun _ : ℕ ↦
        SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj O))
      (fun _ ↦ (SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv _).symm ⟨s.val, s.property⟩)),
      Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ ∃ e : c.pt ≅ ringedSectionLocalization O s,
        (show SheafOfModules.unit _ ⟶ c.pt from c.ι.app 0) ≫ e.hom =
          ringedSectionLocalizationUnit O s
